name: Mango Salsa
headnote: IYENGAR21's note is short: ripe mango, bell pepper, jalapeno and lime make an easy, refreshing salsa that suits fish tacos or chips. A cook's note adds that it is especially good over fish blackened with Cajun seasoning. The editorial section (contributions by Corey Williams) explains that the flavours meld with time, so the salsa is better made a day ahead and should rest at least 30 minutes before serving, and that it keeps about a week refrigerated in a shallow airtight container.
comment_digest: The top review (345 helpful) swaps halved cherry tomatoes for the red pepper, adds avocado, and says to squeeze the juice clinging to the mango pit into the bowl, while stressing that making it early lets the flavours blend. Resting is the step people skip: more than one thought it tasted flat until it had sat, and overnight is better. Salt is the most common missing ingredient, since the recipe includes none; several add it after the salsa sits. Other reported fixes: use a very ripe mango for texture, and cut back to a little over 2 tablespoons of citrus juice total if it turns liquidy or too acidic. The jalapeno divides people, some halving it, others doubling it or using serrano or scotch bonnet. Red onion for green onion is frequent; avocado, tomato, pineapple and mint also work. Canned mango was a poor substitute.
